testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released to the brakes.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much makes them overheat. This heat causes the brakes to fade and work less effectively.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the passenger compartment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drain valves to remove water and compressor oil from air tanks. Water and oil buildup can damage the brakes. Drains should be used every day.

questions.question: What condition should brake linings be in?
questions.explanation: Brake linings must not be loose or covered with oil and grease. They must not be too thin.

questions.question: What prevents wheels from locking up when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup when brakes are applied.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release the parking brake.

questions.question: What are air brakes?

options.text: An effective way to stop large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up so fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi pressure in both systems. Check the air pressure gauges to monitor the pressure.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes. Other vehicles with air brakes built after March 1, 1998 also must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are equipped with:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made after March 1, 1998 also must have ABS.

questions.question: Which of the following is not part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can let air out faster than the compressor can put it back in.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is ____ in a minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not leak more than 4 psi of air per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank on the vehicle.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When the driver presses the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air:

options.text: You should not be concerned as this is normal.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high. If it releases air, there is a problem. Have a mechanic check and fix it.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pressed and the S-cam turns, the S-cam:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Presses the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the brake pedal is pressed, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when tank pressure gets too high. It starts pumping again when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
Prevent the front tires from overheating.
Remove uncertainty when applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves. They were designed to reduce the risk of front wheels skidding. However, research shows these devices are not needed. Leave them in the "normal" position.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving.
Safely exit the roadway and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the roadway and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, you must stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem with the air brake system that needs to be fixed right away.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the air compressor from overheating.
Prevent the front brakes from being used on ice.
Prevent the brakes from being used if downshifting would be more effective.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on a level surface. This is especially important if your vehicle does not have spring brakes, as it prevents the trailer from rolling.
